A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MSMO cross-lingual ABSA research. Text, equations, figures, tables and appendix material support reliable comparison, including identifying content moved into v2's main text.

before.justification: Sections 4.1–4.4 and Appendix A.3 report original ABSA experiments, component ablations, LLM comparisons and parameter-sensitivity results.

after.justification: Sections 4.1–4.5 retain original experimental results. Table 2 additionally reports GPU-memory usage for MSMO and its ablated variants.

M1.justification: The code-switched inputs, adversarial sentence alignment, aspect-level consistency training, combined objective and distillation procedures remain unchanged. The distillation description and equations are relocated from Appendix A.2 into Section 3.3.

E1.justification: Both evaluate SemEval-2016 ABSA with English as source and French, Spanish, Dutch and Russian as targets, retaining the cross-lingual, multilingual and LLM scenarios. The newly cited M-ABSA dataset is not evaluated.

E2.justification: v2 Table 3 adds Equi-XABSA (Lin et al., 2024) to the mBERT and XLM-R comparisons; it is absent from v1 Table 1. Comparator sets in the distillation, multilingual and LLM comparisons remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds approximate GPU-memory consumption as an evaluation measure for the full model and two ablations in Table 2. Existing data counts, Micro-F1 evaluation, backbones, training budgets, learning rates, batch sizes and stated LLM evaluation settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 Table 2 adds a resource-cost comparison examining removal of the language discriminator or consistency training. The existing F1 ablations remain unchanged, and the parameter-sensitivity analysis moves from Appendix A.3 to Section 4.4.

E5.justification: Both versions report average F1 over five runs with different random seeds in Section 3.2. v2 adds no uncertainty estimates, significance tests or revised repeated-run reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds Equi-XABSA results averaging 54.40 and 63.47 for mBERT and XLM-R, respectively, plus GPU-memory estimates. Matched accuracy tables and sensitivity curves retain their results; MSMO averages remain 55.20 and 64.13 in v1 Table 1 and v2 Table 3.

T1.justification: The task definition, Wasserstein/Lipschitz reasoning and Equations 1–8 are mathematically unchanged. Moving the distillation equations into the main text adds no assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the claims about sentence/aspect alignment, multi-objective optimization, distillation and state-of-the-art ABSA performance. The revised title and additional baseline evidence do not redefine the core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 Section 3.2 newly acknowledges computational demands associated with multi-teacher distillation and consistency training. Interpretations of language effects, distillation and parameter tradeoffs, and limitations concerning idiomatic expressions and generalization, remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies an NVIDIA A6000 with 48 GB memory, 42 GB RAM and 120 MB CPU L3 cache. Conversely, it removes the explicit LLM prompt from v1 Appendix A.4/Figure 7, referring readers to Wu et al. (2025b). Most other appendix technical details are relocated.

R1.justification: v2 adds Equi-XABSA, graph-convolutional ABSA work by Wang et al. (2024b), and M-ABSA by Wu et al. (2025a). It condenses the introduction's prior-work discussion and drops Edunov et al. (2018), alongside bibliographic updates and replacements. The central alignment-based positioning remains.

P1.justification: The introduction is substantially shortened, and Appendix subsections A.1–A.3 are integrated into Sections 3.1, 3.3 and 4.4, eliminating the separate appendix structure. The distillation section is reorganized, and title, authorship and acknowledgments are revised, although most method and results prose is retained.

P2.justification: v2 redraws Figures 1 and 3, moves Figures 3–6 and the dataset table into the main text, and reformats Figure 6 into two smaller side-by-side plots. It also removes the prompt figure, adds the GPU-memory table and resizes the main performance comparison.

improvement.justification: Adding the more competitive Equi-XABSA comparison and hardware/memory reporting modestly strengthens assessment of the primary method. These gains outweigh the reduced self-containment of the secondary LLM comparison after prompt removal and the smaller sensitivity plots. The method and original accuracy findings remain unchanged.
